title: Chapter 2 Quiz
description: Test your mastery of the Unity Editor interface, windows, and customization!

questions.question: What key combination allows you to fly through the Scene view in first-person?
questions.explanation: Holding the right mouse button and using WASD enables flythrough mode.

questions.question: What does the 'F' key do when a GameObject is selected?
options: Focuses the Scene view on the object
questions.explanation: Pressing F frames the selected object in the Scene view.

questions.question: Which Scene view toggle hides the skybox and fog?
questions.explanation: The Effects button toggles visual effects like skybox, fog, and post-processing.

questions.question: The Game view's 'Maximize On Play' option makes the game window fullscreen during Play mode.
questions.explanation: When enabled, the Game view expands to fill the entire Editor window while playing.

questions.question: What does the 'Stats' button in the Game view show?
options: Rendering statistics like FPS and batches
questions.explanation: The Stats overlay displays real-time performance data.

questions.question: During Play mode, you can press the _____ button to freeze the current frame and inspect values.
questions.explanation: The Pause button stops execution on the current frame without exiting Play mode.

questions.question: Changes made to a GameObject during Play mode are automatically saved when you stop.
questions.explanation: All Play mode modifications are temporary and discarded upon stopping.

questions.question: How do you create a parent-child relationship between two objects?
options: Rename both with the same prefix
Drag one onto the other in the Hierarchy
questions.explanation: Dragging an object onto another in the Hierarchy parents it.

questions.question: What does the eye icon next to a GameObject in the Hierarchy do?
options: Hides the object in the Scene view only
Makes the object invisible in the Game view
questions.explanation: The eye toggles visibility in the Scene view; the object remains active.

questions.question: How can you prevent accidentally selecting a GameObject in the Scene view?
options: Lock it using the lock icon in the Hierarchy
questions.explanation: The lock icon prevents selection of that object in the Scene view.

questions.question: What component does every single GameObject have?
questions.explanation: Transform defines position, rotation, and scale; it's mandatory.

questions.question: How do you add a new component to a GameObject?
options: Drag a script onto the Scene view
Right-click the object in the Project window
questions.explanation: The 'Add Component' button at the bottom of the Inspector lets you search and attach components.

questions.question: The Inspector's Debug mode can display private fields.
questions.explanation: Debug mode reveals all serialized fields, including private ones marked with [SerializeField].

questions.question: What is the purpose of Component Presets?
options: To create templates for script code
To save a component's configuration and apply it to other objects
questions.explanation: Presets allow you to save component settings as a reusable asset.

questions.question: What does the lock icon in the top‑right of the Inspector do?
options: Keeps the Inspector showing the same object even when selecting others
questions.explanation: Locking the Inspector pins it to the current selection.

questions.question: In the Project window, what does the search query 't:material' do?
questions.explanation: The 't:' filter lets you search by asset type.

questions.question: Where do you change a texture's compression settings?
options: The texture's import settings in the Inspector
questions.explanation: Import settings for a selected asset appear in the Inspector.

questions.question: What are the three message types displayed in the Console?
questions.explanation: The Console categorizes output as Log (white), Warning (yellow), and Error (red).

questions.question: Double‑clicking an error in the Console opens the script at the line that caused it.
questions.explanation: That's a quick way to navigate to the source of the problem.

questions.question: How do you save a custom window layout?
questions.explanation: Use the Layout dropdown in the top‑right of the Editor to save your current arrangement.

questions.question: Where can you change the color tint of Play mode?
questions.explanation: In Preferences → Colors you can customize the Play mode tint and other interface colors.

questions.question: Custom layouts you create are only available for the current Unity project.
questions.explanation: Layouts are saved globally and can be used across all projects.
